Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:31: And we learn in Avot DeRabbi Natan (see chapter 15, section 1): further, Rabbi Eliezer used to say two things: let your fellow's honor be as dear to you as your own; be careful of the honor of his sons and daughters. If you wish that no one take what is yours, do not take what is your fellow's. If you wish that nothing be said against you, do not say anything against your fellow.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:32: Hillel says, be among the disciples of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing peace, loving fellow creatures and drawing them near to Torah. A person is obligated to love his fellow and give him honor - and is this not an a fortiori argument? If the ministering angels, among whom there is no evil inclination, give honor one to another, flesh and blood, among whom there is an evil inclination, all the more so - as it is said (Isaiah 6:3), "and one called to another and said" - one says to his fellow, you are greater than I, and you shall open with the praise of the Omnipresent first.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:33: And we learn in Megillat Chasidim (see Avot DeRabbi Natan Zuta, chapter 2): if you wish to be attached to a friend, do business favorably for him. And a person should not act against his fellow's wishes, and should set aside his own will for the will of others, as we learn in Tractate Shabbat (118b): Rabbi Yosei said, in my days I never acted against my fellows' opinion - I know that I am not a Kohen, but had my fellows told me to go up to the platform [for the priestly blessing], I would have gone up.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:34: There are eight kinds of company among people, and whoever associates with one learns a distinct attribute from it, and these are they: one, whoever associates with kings learns violence and pride. Two, whoever associates with the wealthy learns love of money and the pleasure of this world. Three, whoever associates with the humble learns humility, praise, and thanksgiving. Four, whoever associates with women learns lewdness, desire, laughter, vulgar speech, and every evil thought. Five, whoever associates with the young learns idle talk and jesting, as we learn (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 10), "the chatter of children and sitting in the assemblies of the ignorant remove a person from the world." Six, whoever associates with the wicked learns sins and transgressions and removes repentance from himself. Seven, whoever associates with scoffers learns vanity and falsehood. Eight, whoever associates with the pious and righteous learns kindness and good attributes and inherits the World to Come. A person should always strive to acquire a companion for himself - if he finds one for free, [good], and if not, he should acquire one with money, as we learn (ibid., chapter 1, mishnah 6), "make for yourself a teacher and acquire for yourself a companion." And the sage said, I marvel that a person acquires slaves with his money - how does he not acquire free men with good words from his mouth, since a person acquires companions more through good words than through money?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:35: And the early pious ones would judge every person favorably, and even if they saw a person doing something that appeared to many to be a transgression, they would not disgrace him in their hearts, but would judge him favorably and say, perhaps he did not transgress and his intent was for something else - and they would remove themselves from suspicion, for whoever suspects the upright is afflicted in his own body (Shabbat 97a). And we learn in Tractate Shabbat (127b): our Rabbis taught, whoever judges his fellow favorably is judged favorably [by Heaven] - there was a story of a certain man from Upper Galilee, and so on; see there. And further, a story of Rabbi Yehoshua, and so on; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:36: And we learn in Avot DeRabbi Natan: and judge every person favorably - there was a story of a man who sent his son to his fellow and said, tell him, my father says, lend me a measure of wheat. He went and found him measuring wheat, and he said, I have none. He came and told his father, who said, perhaps it is tithe-wheat. He further said to him, go tell him, my father says, lend me one maneh. He went and found him counting money, and he said, I have none. He came and told his father, who said, perhaps it is a deposit held for someone else. Once they met each other in the marketplace, his fellow said to him, when your son came and found me measuring wheat and I did not give it to you, what did you suspect me of? He said, perhaps it is tithe-wheat. And when he found me counting money, what did you suspect me of? He said, perhaps it is a deposit held for someone else. He said to him, by the [divine] service, so it was, and you did not deviate right or left - and of you it is said, judge every person favorably, and just as you judged me favorably, so may the Holy One, blessed be He, judge you favorably.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:37: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, whoever suspects the upright is afflicted in his own body (Shabbat 97a) - from where do we know this? From Moses, who said (Exodus 4:1), "but behold, they will not believe me" - yet before Heaven it was revealed that they would believe, as it is said (ibid. 4:31), "and the people believed." And since he suspected them, Moses was immediately punished, as it is written (ibid. 4:6), "and the LORD said to him further" - and was there no other thing but tzara'at upon his body? Rather, from here we learn that he was punished for this matter. Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina: a measure of good comes more quickly than a measure of punishment - for there (ibid.), "and he took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous, like snow" - behold, in the measure of punishment there was a delay, and it says "and behold, his hand was leprous," but in the measure of good there was no delay, and it does not say "and behold, his hand," but rather "and behold, it had returned like his own flesh" (ibid. 4:7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:38: And whoever is suspected of something and it is not in him needs to remove himself from the suspicion (see Berachot 31b) - for so we find with Chanah, of whom Eli said (I Samuel 1:14-15), "how long will you be drunk?" and she said to him, no, my lord, I am a woman of sorrowful spirit; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink" - and immediately he said to her, go in peace - from here we learn that when a person is suspected of a matter and it is not in him, one must appease him, and moreover, that one must seek mercy for him, as it is said (ibid. 1:17), "and may the God of Israel grant your request" (Berachot, there). Rabbi Yosei said, may my portion be with whoever is suspected of a matter and it is not in him (Shabbat 118b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:39: And whoever loves his fellow shall always judge him favorably and cover his transgressions, but if he hates him, he shall always judge him unfavorably, even if he has not transgressed, and shall not see merit in him even if he is upright - and from this comes strife with him and he shall seek complaints against him, as it is said (Proverbs 10:12), "hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions" - for out of his hatred of him, his fellow's words are exaggerated in his eyes and he quarrels with him over nothing, and it is the opposite if he loves him, even if his fellow is bound to him by covenant and oath - he shall turn back and break the covenant, since the hatred hidden in his heart shall search out quarrels and stir up strife and all hatred and rivalry, and he shall think in his heart that his fellow too hates him, since he judges the hearts of people to be as evil as his own evil heart, and evil imaginings in his own heart he shall think are so in others' hearts too, and from the evil thought he shall come to action and hate his fellow creatures. A parable of a person walking on a narrow place: if that place is not elevated above the ground, he shall walk quickly and not stumble, and all the more so not fall - but if that place is elevated above the ground, he shall think in his heart that he shall fall to the ground, and from his fear of falling he shall come to actually do so - so too, if he suspects that his fellow hates him too, he too shall hate him more - and whoever entertains an evil thought in his heart shall see that thing he imagined appear to him as true, and it shall become established in his heart and come to action - and so most dreams are nothing but imaginings a person entertains in his heart while awake, which appear to him in a dream.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:40: And we learn in the Midrash: "behold, Pharaoh's army that came out to help you shall return to its land, to Egypt" (Jeremiah 37:7) - why did Pharaoh's army return to Egypt and not come to help Israel? Because they hated them - when they came to the shore of the sea and entertained in their hearts their hatred of Israel, from the evil thought, hatred, and imagining, there appeared to them, on the shore of the sea, inflated wineskins floating on the surface of the water - immediately they turned back, thinking these were the bodies of their own fathers whom the Holy One, blessed be He, had drowned in the sea through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, and they said, it would be a disgrace for us to help our enemies who drowned our fathers in the sea, after having afflicted them with several plagues - from here we learn that hatred leads to enmity and quarrel.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:41: And we learn in the Sifrei: "if men struggle" (Deuteronomy 25:11) - no peace comes forth from struggling - and so it says (Genesis 13:7), "and there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram's cattle and the herdsmen of Lot's cattle" - what caused Lot to separate from Abraham the righteous? Say, strife. And so it says (Deuteronomy 19:17), "then the two men who have the dispute shall stand" - what caused him to be struck? Say, strife. I know only of two men - from where do we know [it applies also to] a mother and daughter, or a man and woman? Scripture says "together" [yachdav, implying any two].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:42: Therefore a person must restrain himself from strife, for whoever restrains himself from strife is honored among people, as it is said (Proverbs 20:3), "it is honor for a man to cease from strife," and it is written (ibid. 12:26), "the righteous has an advantage over his fellow, but the way of the wicked leads them astray." Explanation: the righteous has an advantage over another person, in that the righteous hears his own disgrace and endures his desire and subdues his inclination and is silent, so as not to come to strife and disgrace - "but the way of the wicked leads them astray" - the evil way of the wicked leads them astray, since it is a disgrace in their eyes to hear their own disgrace and be silent, and they stray from the way of reason, so that through this they come to quarrel and murder. And we learn in Chullin (see 89a): Rabbi Ilai said, the world endures only through the merit of one who restrains his mouth at a time of quarrel, as we copied its words above in chapter 3. And the sage said, no person ever disgraced me more than once, for the first time I bear his disgrace, and he shall not disgrace me a second time.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:43: And we learn in the Midrash: "a man of friends [may come] to ruin" (Proverbs 18:24) - whoever wishes to have friends must endure and overlook wrongs against himself, and receive them with a pleasant countenance. Explanation: "lehitro'e'a" [to have friends] is derived from "rei'a" [friend], meaning, he should make himself a friend and companion to every person. Another explanation of "a man of friends," and so on: a person shall never have friends unless he submits before them and breaks his own desire, derived from (Psalms 2:9), "you shall break them with an iron rod" - and then his companionship shall be fine and complete. And the sage said, whoever has not broken his pride before his fellow, and is not always the one insulted by them rather than the insulter of any of them, shall not have friends.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:44: And these good attributes cause a person to have friends more beloved than his own brothers, as it is said (Proverbs 18:24), "but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother," and it is written (ibid. 27:10), "do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend" - if you keep and do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend, you shall not need your brother on the day of your calamity, for your friend shall save you on your day of trouble, being more to you than a brother.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:45: And we learn in Shemot Rabbah (27:1): "better a close neighbor" - this is Jethro - "than a distant brother" - this is Esau. Of Jethro it is written (I Samuel 15:6), "and you showed kindness to all the children of Israel," and so on; of Esau it is written (Deuteronomy 25:17), "remember what Amalek did to you." You find many matters proving that they are written of Esau disparagingly and of Jethro praisingly. Of Esau it is written (Lamentations 5:11), "they afflicted the women in Zion"; of Jethro it is written (Exodus 2:21), "and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses." Of Esau it is written (Psalms 14:4), "who devour my people, they eat bread"; of Jethro it is written (Exodus 2:20), "call him, that he may eat bread." Of Esau it is written (Deuteronomy 25:18), "and did not fear God"; of Jethro it is written (Exodus 18:23), "and God shall command you." Esau abolished sacrifices; of Jethro it is written (Exodus 18:12), "and Jethro took a burnt offering and sacrifices," and so on. Esau heard of their going out and came to fight them, as it is said (Exodus 17:8), "and Amalek came" - while Jethro heard of their good fortune and came to join them, as it is said (Exodus 18:1), "and Jethro heard," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:46: And righteous converts are equal to Israel in love, and are like Israel in all their matters, and it is a positive commandment to love the convert, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:19), "and you shall love the convert." And we learn in the Mechilta: "and you shall not oppress a convert" (Exodus 22:20) - you shall not oppress him with words, and you shall not press him for money. "With words" - that you not say to him, yesterday you were worshipping idols, and pig's meat was still between your teeth, and now you stand and speak against me! And if you oppress him, he shall oppress you, as it is said, "for you were converts in the land of Egypt." From here Rabbi Natan used to say, do not tell your fellow of your own blemish [i.e. do not accuse another of a fault you share].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:47: And we learn in Bava Metzia (59b): our Rabbis taught, whoever oppresses a convert transgresses three prohibitions, and whoever presses him [for money] transgresses two. It is taught, Rabbi Eliezer says, why did the Torah warn concerning the convert in thirty-six places? Because it is written, "for you were converts."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:48: Beloved are converts, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, weighed equal to the holiness of the Sabbath and to holiness from idolatry - for Scripture warned concerning the Sabbath in twenty-eight places, and concerning idolatry in twenty-eight places, and concerning the convert too there is warning in twenty-eight places.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:49: And Israel are called holy, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:2), "for you are a holy people," through being sanctified from idolatry, as it is said (Leviticus 20:7), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" - from forbidden relations, from carcasses and torn animals, from detestable things and creeping things, from impurities. From forbidden relations, as it is said at the end of the section on forbidden relations, "and you shall sanctify yourselves." From carcasses and torn animals, as it is said (Exodus 22:30), "and you shall be men of holiness to Me." From detestable things and creeping things, as it is said at the end of the section on forbidden foods (Leviticus 11:44), "for I am the LORD your God, and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy." From impurities, as it is said (ibid. 16:19), "and shall cleanse it and sanctify it from the impurities of the children of Israel." Even in the future to come, the Holy One, blessed be He, shall sanctify them, as it is said (Ezekiel 37:28), "and the nations shall know that I, the LORD, sanctify Israel" - and so it says, "you shall be holy to Me" in this world, "and I shall separate you from the peoples to be Mine" in the World to Come. Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says, had it said, "and I shall separate the peoples from you," there would have been no possibility of restoration for the nations of the world, and there would have been no opening for any of them to convert - to what is this comparable? To one who sorts bad from good; he does not return to the bad ones, lest he find good among them [i.e. the wording preserves opportunity for conversion].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:50: Beloved are converts, for in every place Scripture warns Israel [with a term], Israel is called by it, converts too are called by it. Israel are called servants, as it is said (Leviticus 25:55), "for the children of Israel are servants to Me," and converts are called servants, as it is said (Isaiah 56:6), "and the sons of the foreigner who join themselves to the LORD, to serve Him and to love the name of the LORD, to be His servants." Israel are called ministers, as it is said (ibid. 61:6), "but you shall be called the priests of the LORD; men shall call you the ministers of our God," and converts are called ministers, as it is said, "and the sons of the foreigner who join themselves to the LORD to serve Him." Israel are called beloved, as it is said (Malachi 1:2), "I have loved you, says the LORD," and converts are called beloved, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:18), "and He loves the convert." Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says, "and those who love Him are like the sun going forth" (Judges 5:31) - whoever loves the Omnipresent, the Omnipresent loves him; of converts it is written, "and He loves the convert," and of the righteous it is written, "and those who love Him are like the sun going forth in its might." And who is greater - one who loves the king, or one whom the king loves? By way of parable, everyone loves their own king, but happy is he whose king loves him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:51: Onkelos the convert asked Rabbi Eliezer, is this the entirety of the affection with which the Holy One, blessed be He, cherished the convert, to give him only bread and clothing (Deuteronomy 10:18)? He said to him, and is that a small thing in your eyes - a thing that that elder [Jacob] pleaded for, saying (Genesis 28:20), "and give me bread to eat," and so on? He came before Rabbi Yehoshua, who began to appease him, saying to him, "bread" here is the bread of Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread," and "clothing" is Torah, as it is said (Isaiah 3:6), "clothing, be our leader." And moreover, their [the converts'] daughters marry into the priesthood and bear priests, and they merit "bread and clothing" - "bread" is the showbread, and "clothing" is the priestly garments - this is within the Sanctuary; and from where also outside its bounds? "Bread" is the challah [dough-offering], and "clothing" is the first shearing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:52: Of Israel "covenant" is said, as it is said (Genesis 17:13), "and My covenant shall be in your flesh," and of converts "covenant" is said, as it is said (Isaiah 56:4), "and hold fast to My covenant." Of Israel "favor" [ratzon] is said, as it is said (Exodus 28:38), "for favor for them before the LORD," and of converts "favor" is said, as it is said (Isaiah 56:7), "their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be favorably [accepted] on My altar." Of Israel "guarding" is said, as it is said (Psalms 121:3), "behold, He who guards Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps," and of converts "guarding" is said, as it is said (ibid. 146:9), "the LORD guards the converts." And so you find converts among the four groups who answer and say before Him who spoke and the world came into being (cf. Isaiah 44:5): this one shall say, I am the LORD's - these are Israel. And this one shall call himself by the name of Jacob - these are righteous converts. And this one shall write with his hand, "to the LORD" - these are penitents. And [this one] shall be surnamed by the name of Israel - these are those who fear Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:53: Rabbi says, a convert who comes to convert is as though he had done a kindness to all of Israel - for so Saul said to the sons of Jethro (I Samuel 15:6), "and you showed kindness to all the children of Israel" - and is there anyone who could do a kindness to all those thousands and myriads? Rather, since he converted among them, [it is as though everyone] said (Exodus 18:10), "blessed is the LORD who saved you" - as though he had done a kindness to all of them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:54: Beloved are converts, for the Holy One, blessed be He, adds to their name - for so you find with Jethro: at first he was called only Yeter, as it is said (Exodus 4:18), "and he returned to Yeter his father-in-law," and once he converted, he was called Yitro. And so, whoever rises to greatness has something added to his name, as it is said (Genesis 17:5), "and your name shall be Abraham," and likewise (Numbers 13:16), "and Moses called Hoshea son of Nun, Yehoshua." And there are some whose names are diminished because of their evil deeds - for Ahab, the false prophet, was called Achav [without the extra letter], as it is said (Jeremiah 29:22-23), "may God make you like Zedekiah and like Achav."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:55: A convert who converts is given reward as though he had toiled in Torah all his days, as it is said (Numbers 10:29), "come with us, and we shall do good to you" - like one of us. And when he came to Joshua, and the fertile land of Jericho and all its produce were set aside for the Temple, he said, whoever helps build the Temple within its boundary shall take this in place of [a portion of] the Temple - and who ate it all those years? The sons of Jethro, as it is said (Judges 1:16), "and the children of the Kenite, Moses's father-in-law, went up from the city of palm trees" - teaching that they dwelt there as long as Joshua lived, since they were available there to learn Torah - and they arose and departed from there, as it is said, "went up from the city of palm trees" - and they went about seeking someone to teach them Torah, and found Ya'betz and settled near him, as it is said (I Chronicles 2:55), "and the families of scribes who dwelt at Ya'betz: the Tir'atim, the Shim'atim, the Sukatim - these are the Kenites," and so on. "Tir'atim" - because they would cry out [matri'in] in their supplication and be answered. "Shim'atim" - because their prayer was heard [nishma'at]. "Sukatim" - because they would shelter [mesakhin] and protect all of Israel. Come and see how great was the righteousness of the sons of Jethro - for Yonadav son of Rechav heard from the mouth of the prophet in the Temple that it was destined to be destroyed, and he decreed upon his children three decrees, and these are they: one, that they not drink wine; two, that they not build houses; three, that they not plant vineyards - as it is said (Jeremiah 35:6), "and they said, we shall not drink wine, for Yonadav son of Rechav, our father, commanded us." Rabbi Yochanan says, the covenant made with the sons of Jethro is greater than the covenant made with David - for that covenant is conditional: "if your children keep My covenant... and if not, then I will visit their transgression with the rod" (Psalms 89:31-33) - but the covenant made with Yonadav is not conditional, as it is said (Jeremiah 35:19), "there shall not be cut off a man for Yonadav son of Rechav," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:56: And further we learn in Shemot Rabbah: "and Jethro heard" - this is what is written (Jeremiah 16:19), "LORD, my strength, my fortress, and my refuge" - Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He, when You performed miracles for us at the sea, we said, "my strength and my song is the LORD" (Exodus 15:2) - Rachav heard and came to attach herself to You, as it is said (Joshua 2:10), "for we have heard how [the LORD] dried up," and so on - hence "the LORD, my strength and my fortress." When You performed miracles in the days of Solomon, as it is written (I Samuel 2:10), "and He gives strength to His king," the Queen of Sheba came and praised You, saying (I Kings 10:9), "blessed be the LORD your God." When You brought us out of Egypt, You gave us the Torah, called "strength," as it is said (Psalms 29:11), "the LORD gives strength to His people" - Jethro heard and came and attached himself to You. Hence (Jeremiah, ibid.), "to You the nations shall come from the ends of the earth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:57: And we learn in Bamidbar Rabbah, to what are converts compared, in relation to Israel? To a shepherd who was tending his flock, and a ewe fled from the field and came and entered his flock, and it was more beloved to him than the rest - because he had purchased his own sheep with money, while this one he did not purchase with money, but rather it came of its own accord and entered his flock. So too Israel: how many signs, wonders, and miracles did the Holy One, blessed be He, perform for them before they accepted the Torah - but this convert comes of his own accord to enter beneath the wings of the Shechinah, without sign or wonder.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:58: Beloved are converts, for all the Patriarchs called themselves converts. Abraham, peace be upon him, said (Genesis 23:4), "I am a stranger and a sojourner among you." Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 2:22), "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land." King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 39:13), "for I am a sojourner with You." And even Isaac our father, peace be upon him, is called a sojourner, as it is said (Genesis 26:6), "and Isaac dwelt in Gerar [related to ger, sojourner]." And even Jacob our father, peace be upon him, is called a sojourner (ibid. 47:4), "to sojourn in the land we have come" - our fathers called themselves sojourners, as it is written (I Chronicles 29:15), "for we are sojourners before You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:59: Beloved are converts, for because of them the Holy One, blessed be He, delayed with Abraham's circumcision until he reached ninety-nine years - for had Abraham circumcised himself at ten or twenty years of age, there would have been a fixed limit for the matter, and no convert could convert except up to that measure - but the Holy One, blessed be He, delayed ninety-nine years, until he completed a hundred, in order to give an opening for all who come into the world to convert. Therefore a person must love converts and have compassion on them, and say, it is fitting for this one, who left his father, mother, family, and native land and came to enter beneath the wings of the Shechinah, that mercy be had on him. And whoever does not have mercy on him, no mercy is had on him from Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:60: And whoever is cruel and has no mercy, and hates his fellow creatures, and strikes his fellow with the whip of his tongue and the words of his mouth, his sin and his punishment are exceedingly great - all the more so one who raises his hand against his fellow, and all the more so with a sword or a spear - as we learn in Sanhedrin (see 58b): Rabbi Chanina said, whoever slaps his fellow's cheek is as though he slaps the cheek of the Shechinah, as it is said (Proverbs 20:25), "it is a snare for a man to devour [swallow] the holy thing rashly."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:61: And we learn in Midrash Mishlei (22:11): "he who loves purity of heart, whose speech is gracious," and so on - meaning, whoever loves his companions in his heart and speaks softly to them with his lips is fit to be a friend to the king. And Rabbi Chananel, of blessed memory, explained "his fellow, the king" - that his words are heard more than the king's own words, for the king's words are heeded out of fear, but the words of the pure of heart are heeded because of the grace of his lips. And by the response of one's mouth the lover is recognized, just as the hater is recognized by his lips, as it is said (Proverbs 26:24), "with his lips the hater disguises himself." Another explanation: "with his lips the hater disguises himself" - meaning, he does not show the hatred in his heart, but rather makes his words gracious, though within him lies deceit - and the explanation of "disguises" [yinacher] is that he shows with his mouth the opposite of what is in his heart, as in "and he disguised himself [vayitnaker] to them" (Genesis 42:7), and "a child too is known [yitnaker] by his deeds" (Proverbs 20:11).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:62: And a person must honor his fellow even if he is younger than him in wisdom and years, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, elaborated on this matter and said (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 10): Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua says, let the honor of your student be as dear to you as your own, the honor of your fellow like the reverence of your teacher, and the reverence of your teacher like the reverence of Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:63: And a person is obligated to instruct his fellow and guide him in the good way, and love him as his own soul - and if he asked something of his fellow and he did not do his wish, he should not blame him. And the sage said, if I requested something of my fellow and he did not fulfill my request, I would say, my request was not fulfilled because of my own unworthiness, and I forgive my fellow for not fulfilling it. And he should not intend his fellow's benefit except for the sake of Heaven, not so that people praise him. And if his fellow sins against him or does him some improper thing, even greatly distressing him, he should remove anger from his heart and forgive him immediately. And if he himself sins against his fellow, he should send many friends [to intercede] until he appeases him, and even his enemy who greatly distressed him, he should repay good for evil. And know that a person's harm in this world comes only from the aspect of his own sins, and it is not in a person's power to distress his fellow unless he has assistance from above through the other's own sin - and therefore he should blame his fellow only for his own sin and transgression, as it is said (Isaiah 50:1), "behold, for your iniquities you were sold."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:64: A person should always draw near his lovers and distance himself from his haters, and listen to and accept the counsel of his lovers, as we learn in Yevamot (62b): whoever loves his neighbors, draws his relatives near, marries his sister's daughter, and lends to the poor in his time of need - of him Scripture says (Isaiah 58:9), "then you shall call, and the LORD shall answer." And even if his relatives curse him and disgrace him, he should listen to them, for they intend his own good, as we learn in the chapter "Chelek" (Sanhedrin 105b): Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said, what is the meaning of what is written (Proverbs 27:6), "faithful are the wounds of a lover," and so on? Better is the curse that Achiyah the Shilonite cursed Israel with, than the blessing with which Balaam blessed them. Achiyah cursed them with a reed, as it is said (I Kings 14:15), "and the LORD shall strike Israel as a reed sways in the water" - just as this reed stands in a place of water, and its trunk is renewed and its roots are many, and even if all the winds come and blow upon it, it goes and comes with them, and once they are still it stands in its place - so too Israel. But Balaam the wicked blessed them with a cedar - just as this cedar does not stand in a place of water and its trunk is not renewed, and once a south wind blows upon it, it uproots it and turns it upon its face - and this was the intent of Balaam the wicked, even in his blessings, to uproot the enemies of Israel [i.e., ironically, Israel themselves, cursed via blessing]. And at a time when love and brotherhood dwell in Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, comforts Zion and builds Jerusalem, and then there shall be peace and tranquility in your palaces, as it is said (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and my friends, let me now say, peace be within you" - to this point. And some of the teachings he, peace be upon him, brought I have skipped in copying, since they are well known and I did not wish to be so lengthy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 4:65: Up to here has reached the discussion of the mitzvah of loving one's fellows, along the lines of what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in the Midrashim. Further, I have seen fit to speak of the matter of loving one's fellows by way of the secret, according to what is understood from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar, and we shall explain this matter in a chapter of its own, and further matters that are great causes for nullifying anger, in order to give some space between chapter and chapter:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 5:1: The reason for loving one's fellows by way of the secret is that, since it is true and agreed by all that all souls are emanated from a high place, one must love all the souls of his fellows in that they are a portion of God above, in the same existence by which he loves his own soul - and just as the supernal Godhead is unified in the ultimate unity, so too souls above have no envy, rivalry, or hatred among them, God forbid, for these attributes are external attributes from the external husk - but in holiness everything is in love, as we have elaborated in the Gate of Love, chapter 1 and chapter 6; see there. And although our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Batra 75a, Zohar Parashat Bereishit, page 39a) that in the lower Garden of Eden each one is scorched by his fellow's canopy, this is not from hatred, but rather he is ashamed, thinking that he should have been worthy of attaining that level, for the supernal light to shine upon him more than what he has - for all the desire of the righteous in the Garden of Eden is this. It follows that this is an envy that leads to love of the Name, and he loves his fellow who merited that level through his own deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 5:2: Now, from two aspects one must love his fellow: the first, from the aspect of the soul; the second, from the aspect of the body - and concerning these two aspects, one can say the prophet said (Malachi 2:10), "have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously, each with his brother?" And Rashi, of blessed memory, explained: "have we not all one father" - this is Jacob our father, peace be upon him. And certainly this aspect is from the aspect of the body - for Jacob our father, peace be upon him, his bed was complete, without any admixture of the husk, and he merited to beget twelve tribes who produced seventy souls, all in holiness, so that not one of them went outside - and therefore Israel were then separated from the other nations; however, "Jacob is the cord of His inheritance," as explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 1 - and therefore it is forbidden for us to intermarry with the other seventy nations. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei, page 70b), which we copied in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4, saying, happy are the righteous, and so on, their body is holy, their soul is holy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 5:3: "Has not one God created us" - "created us" is from the aspect of the soul, for the Creator, blessed be He, from His own spirituality, creates the souls, which are spiritual like Him, as they, of blessed memory, explained (Niddah 31a), "three partners in a person," and so on - and the soul is equal to the Holy One, blessed be He, in five things, as explained in the first chapter of Berachot (10a) concerning the five times "bless the LORD, O my soul" is said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 5:4: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 246b) it explained "one God created us" as an allusion to two supernal [Names] - these are its words: another explanation, "and he dreamed, and behold, a ladder" (Genesis 28:12) - the Ra'aya Meheimna: my Master, "sulam" [ladder] ascends [in gematria] to all the letters [of a Name] - thus you act, to ascend above all creatures, in order to ascend to the Name in Yud-Kei, Vav-Kei, in which is Yud-Yud-Yud, whose numerical value is 30 [samekh-lamed], for at first you were in the Name Yud-Kei-Aleph, Vav-Kei-Aleph, which is Yud-Aleph-Aleph-Aleph, in the thirteen measures of mercy, which is ECHAD [one] - now you shall ascend in EL [God], which is YAI [Yud-Aleph-Yud] - for two Names testify, "have not one God [EL ECHAD] created us?" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 5:5: And when you examine what is explained in the Tikkunim, that these two Names mentioned are, this one the body and this one the soul, and what is explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 7, our words here shall become settled for you: that in the allusion of these words there is a partnership for the creation of souls.
